versions.exchangeRate: All US dollar denominated tariff will be recovered in Indian Rupees after conversion of charges in US dollar terms into its equivalent Indian Rupees at the Reference rate notified by the Reserve Bank of India or the market buying rate notified by State Bank of India as may be specified from time to time whichever is higher on date of arrival of the vessel.

charges.label: Port dues
conditions: Foreign ships pay on each entry; coastal ships pay once in 30 days, valid for three entries.
Half rate for ships calling only for provisions, water or bunkers; 75% in ballast leaving laden; 50% with no cargo work.

charges.label: Pilotage and towage
conditions: Includes the port's pilot, the required tugs and launches, and mooring crew for one inward and one outward movement.
Cold moves cost double.

charges.label: Berth hire
conditions: A minimum per hour applies (US$ 10.80 or 8.64 foreign; Rs. 296 or 237 coastal).
Berth hire stops 2 hours after the ship is ready to sail if it cannot sail for port reasons.

notes.text: Kamarajar Port Limited's consolidated Scale of Rates has no overall effective date; the latest amendment to vessel-related charges is for container vessels from 4 June 2019, and the latest amendment of any kind is from July 2025. No 2026 revision was found, so these rates may be out of date.
Pilotage rates are per GT by size band with no statement that they apply incrementally, so the whole tonnage is charged at its band's rate.
The berth hire table covers coal berths, the general cargo berth and finger jetties. Container vessels at the BOT container terminals are not covered by it, so container berth hire is not priced.
The two one-page annexes (coastal cars, granite blocks) are cargo promotions and are not entered.

Dry bulk ships at anchorage pay nothing for the first 48 hours, then per GT: Rs. 0.023 / US$ 0.001 from 49 to 96 hours, Rs. 0.046 / US$ 0.002 from 97 to 144 hours and Rs. 0.092 / US$ 0.004 beyond 144 hours. The Scale of Rates doesn't say 'per hour'; Trade Notice 6 of 21 May 2016, which introduced these slabs, is reported to say 'per GRT per hour or part thereof', but the port's website refused downloads on 25 October 2026, so anchorage is not priced until it is checked.
Kamarajar's schedule says cargo it doesn't list pays the rate of nearby major ports; Berthwise doesn't apply other ports' rates.
